discovery: Prediction and discovery of the spin Hall and inverse spin Hall effects, enabling the generation and electrical detection of pure spin currents
motivation: In 1971 Dyakonov (with the late V. I. Perel) predicted that spin-orbit coupling deflects electrons of opposite spin to opposite sides of a conductor, so a charge current produces a transverse pure spin current. The idea lay dormant for three decades until Awschalom's group optically imaged spin accumulation at semiconductor edges in 2004, establishing the spin Hall effect experimentally. In 2006 Saitoh demonstrated the inverse effect, converting spin currents, injected by spin pumping, into measurable voltages. Together these discoveries turned spin-orbit coupling into a practical tool for creating and detecting spin currents without ferromagnets or magnetic fields. They underpin spin-orbit torque switching in magnetic memory, spin Seebeck and magnon transport experiments in magnetic insulators, and the detection of spin currents in antiferromagnets. The results have been reproduced in hundreds of laboratories and materials, and they define a whole field of modern condensed matter physics.
